sections.1:
Archlin is undertaking a Phase 1 supply management initiative for its specialty chemicals manufacturing business to address current planning limitations and improve supply chain execution readiness. Archlin’s current planning maturity is characterized by Excel-based planning with no centralized platform, creating constraints in inventory planning, forecast visibility, and the ability to respond consistently to supply requirements. The Phase 1 scope is focused on supply management and is aligned to Archlin’s need to strengthen planning discipline around inventory, raw material availability, and visibility across supply planning decisions.

Archlin’s current-state challenges include poor inventory planning, high inventory, poor forecast visibility, and raw material shortages. These conditions indicate that Archlin’s planning process requires improved structure, greater transparency, and better integration with the enterprise planning and transactional environment. Archlin’s ERP system is SAP S/4HANA, and the future-state supply management design for Phase 1 must therefore consider how planning information, supply signals, inventory inputs, and execution-relevant data are aligned with SAP S/4HANA as the system of record. Specific integration design details, data objects, process touchpoints, and technical connectivity are TBD unless confirmed in later source documents.

The solution direction for Archlin’s Phase 1 investment is to move from fragmented Excel-based planning toward a more centralized planning approach for supply management. Within the confirmed scope, the emphasis is on enabling better planning visibility, improving the quality of inventory-related decisions, and supporting more reliable supply planning outcomes. The implementation should focus on the planning processes and data required to address Archlin’s identified pain points, including inventory levels, forecast visibility constraints, and raw material shortages. Any detailed capability design, planning hierarchy, user role model, workflow definition, scenario structure, or exception-management process remains TBD where not explicitly provided in the available Archlin source context.

For Archlin, the Blueprint establishes the foundation for translating Phase 1 supply management objectives into an implementable enterprise solution design. It captures the business context, current-state limitations, and expected planning direction needed to support a future-state supply management process. The document is intended to guide implementation alignment between business requirements, SAP S/4HANA data dependencies, planning process design, and expected operating outcomes. The Blueprint should therefore serve as the controlled reference point for confirming scope, clarifying assumptions, documenting design decisions, and identifying areas where Archlin-specific information is still TBD.

The intended outcome of Archlin’s Phase 1 supply management implementation is improved planning effectiveness in the areas directly linked to the stated business issues. Success should be reflected through better inventory planning, improved visibility to forecast-related supply requirements, and reduced exposure to raw material shortages. As the implementation progresses, Archlin will need to validate the detailed process design, data readiness, integration requirements, and operational adoption model required to move from the current Excel-based environment to a centralized planning capability for supply management.
sections.1.3:
The purpose of this Blueprint Document is to define the Phase 1 supply management blueprint for Archlin’s specialty chemicals manufacturing planning environment. Archlin currently performs planning through Excel-based processes with no centralized planning platform, which contributes to poor inventory planning, high inventory, poor forecast visibility, and raw material shortages.

This section establishes the intent of the Blueprint as the reference point for documenting Archlin’s current planning challenges, the intended Phase 1 supply management solution direction, the implementation focus, and the business outcomes expected from improving supply planning discipline. The Blueprint is intended to support alignment between Archlin’s SAP S/4HANA ERP environment and the future supply management planning process by describing how planning requirements, process expectations, and supply chain pain points will be addressed within the approved Phase 1 scope.

For Archlin, the Blueprint serves the following purposes:

Document the current state of planning, including Excel-based planning, lack of centralized planning capability, poor inventory planning, limited forecast visibility, and raw material shortages.

Define the Phase 1 supply management scope for Archlin in a manner that is specific to the specialty chemicals manufacturing operating context.

Provide a structured basis for solution design decisions related to supply planning, inventory visibility, and planning process improvement.

Support implementation alignment between business planning needs and Archlin’s SAP S/4HANA ERP environment.

Establish a common reference for evaluating expected outcomes, including stronger planning effectiveness, improved inventory visibility and control, and reduction of avoidable supply chain costs associated with suboptimal inventory decisions.
sections.1.4:
Archlin’s Phase 1 investment is focused on supply management for its specialty chemicals manufacturing business. Archlin currently uses SAP S/4HANA as its ERP system and operates with Excel-based planning and no centralized planning platform. In the current state, Archlin experiences poor inventory planning, high inventory, poor forecast visibility, raw material shortages, and delays in monthly planning cycles caused by manual Excel processes. These current-state constraints limit Archlin’s ability to maintain consistent supply visibility, manage inventory targets effectively, and respond efficiently to recurring material availability issues.

Within Phase 1, Archlin plans to implement Kinaxis RapidResponse capabilities for supply management, with the broader planned solution context including Demand Planning, Supply Planning, and Inventory Optimization. The Phase 1 supply management scope is intended to establish a centralized planning approach that supports constrained supply planning, material shortage identification, capacity planning, inventory target management, and exception-based supply visibility. Archlin’s supply and inventory planning process will be integrated with demand planning outputs so that supply decisions can be informed by improved forecast visibility and planning inputs across regions.

The solution will support Archlin in generating constrained supply plans using demand and supply inputs, identifying material shortages, and supporting capacity planning activities. Exception-based alerts will help Archlin’s supply planners focus attention on recurring raw material shortage issues. Scenario analysis will allow Archlin to evaluate planning alternatives before committing to supply decisions, supporting a more structured response to changing supply conditions and inventory risks. For inventory planning, the solution will support definition of safety stock policies, calculation of inventory targets, monitoring of excess inventory, tracking of inventory turns, and optimization of stock across locations.

The implementation approach for this section of scope should therefore be anchored to Archlin’s supply management priorities rather than treated as a technical deployment alone. Baseline measurements should be established for the inventory planning and supply management indicators Archlin chooses to manage, and the same metrics should be monitored after implementation to confirm realized value. Because Archlin source documents do not provide specific current-state values, target thresholds, reporting cadence, business owners, validation methods, detailed target-state integration architecture, site-level deployment scope, quantified savings, or implementation timeline, these items remain TBD and should be confirmed during blueprint validation.

The expected business outcome for Archlin is improved planning effectiveness through centralized supply and inventory planning, stronger visibility to supply constraints, better management of inventory targets, and improved ability to respond to raw material shortages. The value of Phase 1 should be assessed by the extent to which Archlin can translate poor inventory planning into measurable supply chain outcomes, including improved inventory visibility and control, reduced avoidable supply chain costs associated with suboptimal inventory decisions, and improved responsiveness within the supply management process.

sections.4:
Archlin operates as a specialty chemicals manufacturer using SAP S/4HANA as its ERP system, while its current planning process remains Excel-based and lacks a centralized planning platform across North America and Europe. This operating model creates material planning constraints for Archlin, including poor inventory planning, high inventory, poor forecast visibility, raw material shortages, and delays in monthly planning cycles. Demand planners currently spend significant time consolidating forecasts from multiple regions, and forecast accuracy is approximately 68%, contributing to higher-than-target inventory levels and reduced visibility for supply and inventory decisions.

Archlin’s Phase 1 scope is focused on supply management, with the implementation objective to establish planning capabilities that support demand planning, supply planning, and inventory optimization. The target solution is expected to provide a single source of planning data, improve planner productivity, and support measurable improvements in forecast accuracy, inventory reduction, and planning cycle efficiency. The solution direction includes the implementation of Kinaxis RapidResponse for Demand Planning, Supply Planning, and Inventory Optimization, integrated with Archlin’s SAP S/4HANA environment.

From a demand planning perspective, Archlin requires the ability to generate statistical baseline forecasts, support planner forecast overrides, track forecast history and changes, and support multiple forecast hierarchies. Collaboration capabilities are required to allow sales teams to provide forecast input, enable approval workflows, and provide forecast comparison reporting. These capabilities are intended to improve collaborative forecasting and visibility across regions, which business users emphasized as a key need during blueprint discussions.

Archlin’s supply planning requirements include generating constrained supply plans, identifying material shortages, supporting capacity planning, providing exception-based alerts, and enabling scenario analysis. These capabilities directly address recurring raw material shortage issues identified by supply planners and are expected to improve Archlin’s ability to identify constraints, evaluate supply responses, and manage exceptions with better visibility.

Archlin’s inventory planning requirements include defining safety stock policies, calculating inventory targets, monitoring excess inventory, tracking inventory turns, and optimizing stock across locations. These requirements are aligned to Archlin’s stated objective to improve inventory planning, reduce excess inventory, increase planning visibility, and enable more responsive management of raw material shortages.

The required interfaces for the planning implementation include Product Master, Customer Master, Sales Orders, Inventory Balances, Purchase Orders, and Production Orders. The data refresh frequency is every 4 hours. These integrations are expected to support more current planning data availability and reduce dependency on manual consolidation activities within the planning cycle.

The expected business outcomes for Archlin include forecast accuracy greater than 85%, inventory reduction greater than 15%, planning cycle reduction greater than 30%, improved planner productivity, and a single source of planning data. Leadership expects measurable improvements in forecast accuracy and inventory reduction within six months of go-live. For Phase 1 supply management, these outcomes establish the basis for improving forecast visibility, reducing excess inventory, and supporting more responsive supply and inventory decisions.
